The *Selattheragāthā* (Thag 16.6) is a collection of verses in the *Theragāthā* attributed to the elder Sela [SuttaCentral]. 

SuttaCentral records direct canonical parallels to the verses in the *Sela Sutta* of the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 92) and the *Sutta Nipāta* (Snp 3.7, *Sela Sutta*), as well as a passage-level connection to the *Sabhiya Sutta* (Snp 3.6) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates these relationships, identifying substantial Pali-internal text reuse with both MN 92 (spanning segments §0.4–20.5) and Snp 3.7, as well as shared passages with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.10, *Vaṇṇabhaṇanapañha*), and the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with the Sanskrit *Bhaiṣajyavastu* and the Tibetan Vinayavastu (*'Dul ba gzhi*, D0001-3), with further automatic alignments to the Tibetan *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and *Karmaśataka*, and the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) [DharmaNexus].

SuttaCentral catalogs nine modern translations across eight languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. No discussion of the text was found in the surveyed secondary literature dossier, where all matching hits represented irrelevant homographs [1; 2; 3; 4].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
